title: Intergroup Competition Promotes Intragroup Cooperation: A Meta-Analysis of Social Dilemmas
opposition_rationale: competition is between groups while cooperation is within group; valid level-switch contrast rather than literal antonymy

title: Intergroup conflict: individual, group, and collective interests
opposition_rationale: between-group conflict and within-group cooperation can be represented at distinct levels

title: Deterrence and International Conflict: Empirical Findings and Theoretical Debates
opposition_rationale: credible threat/preparation is distinct from realized war; outcome is conflict prevention
opposite_construct: absence/prevention of attack or crisis escalation
boundary_conditions: does not justify war itself causing peace

title: Domestic Discontent and the External Use of Force
opposition_rationale: domestic discontent -> external force is not itself an opposite-producing relation unless domestic stabilization/support is measured
boundary_conditions: requires explicit domestic outcome to qualify as OCI
exclusion_reason: exposure and outcome are not functional opposites under strict schema

title: The Security Dilemma: A Conceptual Analysis
opposition_rationale: security-seeking measures can reduce security through reciprocal strategic response
mediator: other actor threat perception and response

title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
opposition_rationale: more formal options can reduce motivation/satisfaction to choose
moderator: substantial between-study heterogeneity; no sufficient conditions identified
counterevidence: mean effect virtually zero across 63 conditions

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
opposition_rationale: option quantity can worsen choice outcomes under identifiable moderators
moderator: choice-set complexity; task difficulty; preference uncertainty; decision goal

title: The Autonomy Paradox: The Implications of Mobile Email Devices for Knowledge Professionals
opposition_rationale: short-run flexibility/control is contrasted with longer-run reduced ability to disconnect

title: Self-Determination Theory Applied to Health Contexts: A Meta-Analysis
opposition_rationale: primarily tests beneficial associations of autonomy support/motivation rather than an opposite-producing effect
counterevidence: autonomy-related constructs generally associated with beneficial outcomes

title: Self-Determination Theory and Workplace Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
opposition_rationale: tests adaptive pathways of need support and autonomous motivation

title: Homo Heuristicus: Why Biased Minds Make Better Inferences
opposition_rationale: using less information/computation can improve predictive accuracy under specified environments

title: Homo Ignorans: Deliberately Choosing Not to Know
opposition_rationale: reviews functional reasons for not knowing but ignorance does not necessarily cause improved performance or power

title: Does ignorance love company? The social dynamics of information avoidance
opposition_rationale: findings mainly show information sharing increases awareness/prosocial choice and avoidance can undermine prosociality
exclusion_reason: negative control for generalized ignorance benefit

title: Implications of Rational Inattention
opposition_rationale: limited processing can make selective attention rational but does not by itself establish ignorance causing strength

title: Social Value of Public Information
opposition_rationale: more public information can reduce social welfare under coordination/private-information conditions

title: The Constructive, Destructive, and Reconstructive Power of Social Norms
opposition_rationale: energy-conservation message can increase energy use among already low-use households
opposite_construct: increase rather than decrease in energy use
boundary_conditions: boomerang among low-use households; injunctive message eliminated it

title: Do descriptive norms messaging interventions backfire? Protocol for a systematic review of the boomerang effect
opposition_rationale: protocol directly defines regression to undesirable behavior after norm messaging as boomerang
notes: useful taxonomy source; not outcome evidence

title: Iatrogenic effects of psychosocial interventions for substance use disorders: prevalence, predictors, prevention
opposition_rationale: treatment/prevention intended to improve substance-use outcomes can be followed by deterioration or increased use in subgroups
causal_claim_strength: mixed; review warns deterioration not always attributable causally
counterevidence: review explicitly distinguishes deterioration from demonstrated treatment causation

title: Psychological Treatments That Cause Harm
opposition_rationale: therapeutic intervention can worsen the condition it intends to improve

title: Effects of normative feedback for drinkers who consume less than the norm: Dodging the boomerang
opposition_rationale: directly tests whether a drinking-reduction intervention increases drinking among lighter drinkers
study_design: secondary analyses of four randomized intervention samples
counterevidence: no evidence of boomerang in any of four samples

title: Jevons’ Paradox revisited: The evidence for backfire from improved energy efficiency
opposition_rationale: efficiency intended to reduce resource use may under full backfire increase total energy use
boundary_conditions: full Jevons backfire difficult to test; evidence not conclusive

title: The road to hell is paved with good intentions: A review and research agenda on rebound effects and win–win strategies
opposition_rationale: resource/financial efficiency strategies can trigger rebound that offsets intended environmental benefit
opposite_construct: offset or reversal of environmental improvement
boundary_conditions: rebound magnitude ranges from partial offset to possible backfire

title: Braess' paradox: Some new insights
opposition_rationale: adding network capacity/link can increase total system travel time
opposite_construct: higher rather than lower travel cost
moderator: travel demand and congestion function parameters

title: Bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review of the traffic paradoxes (1968–2022)
opposition_rationale: reviews formal and applied cases where network additions can raise travel cost

title: Safe development paradox: evidence and methodological insights from a systematic review
opposition_rationale: protective risk-reduction infrastructure can increase long-run exposure/risk via development and perceived safety

title: Toward a Theory of Paradox: A Dynamic Equilibrium Model of Organizing
opposition_rationale: framework concerns contradictory interdependent demands but does not require X causally producing its functional opposite
exclusion_reason: umbrella competitor; contradiction/interdependence is broader than directional causal inversion

title: Dynamic Decision Making: A Model of Senior Leaders Managing Strategic Paradoxes
opposition_rationale: exploration/exploitation tensions are opposing demands but paper focuses on management of both rather than one causing its opposite
exclusion_reason: paradox management rather than opposite-producing causal relation

title: Over-optimization of academic publishing metrics: observing Goodhart's Law in action
opposition_rationale: optimizing a measure as target can reduce the measure's validity/usefulness
opposite_construct: reduced metric validity as measure of impact
boundary_conditions: causal attribution weaker than randomized/quasi-experimental designs

title: Core capabilities and core rigidities: A paradox in managing new product development
opposition_rationale: organizational strengths/capabilities can become rigidities constraining innovation under changed task/environment demands
boundary_conditions: new product/process development and environmental fit

title: Counterfinality: On the Increased Perceived Instrumentality of Means to a Goal
opposition_rationale: a means harming an alternative goal increases perceived instrumentality for a focal goal; outcome is not the functional opposite of the exposure under the strict OCI definition
moderator: importance of focal and alternative goals
exclusion_reason: closest umbrella competitor but not strict opposite-producing relation
